items.title: Earl Watkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 7, 2002
items.q: Even Duke’s band, there was an exodus out of his band with Johnny Hodges and Lawrence Brown and all those guys and they went out with Norman Granz.

ctx.x: So there is always a controversy. I mean even if you read history in New Orleans, how there seemed to be controversies. You have the different schools. As I guess each age has its musical culture, musical taste, their fad, or whatever you want to call it. So I’m speaking for myself. I came up in the big band era. Then when bebop came in I was just fascinated with it, just absolutely fascinated with it. The improvisation, the tempos, the soloists, the independence that the drummers had. It was just fascinating. So…

And we used to get calls from the management, “We’d like to know if you could tell us the band that played there.
